> 將欲歙之，必固張之；將欲弱之，必固強之；將欲廢之，必固興之；將欲取之，必固與之.

This is the most misread chapter in the book, and the misreading comes entirely from one character.

Four parallel clauses, too neat to be accidental: to close it, first let it open; to weaken it, first let it strengthen; to abolish it, first let it rise; to take it, first give it.

That sure a pattern reads like a manual. Which is why people have read it as strategy — fatten it, then harvest.

That reading has to be blocked, and it has to be blocked from the text, not from the argument.

The character carrying the whole ambiguity is 固.

Read as "originally, already" — the four clauses describe how things actually work. Read as "deliberately" — they describe a technique. One character's difference, and Laozi goes from a man watching heaven to a man playing a board.

## 固 as "already"

固 in classical usage normally means firm, fixed, or 本來 — as it was to begin with. 必固張之: it must already be open before it closes.

Read this way, the four clauses are not instructions to anyone. They are observations about a regularity: the opening is the condition of the closing, not a step toward it.

No one arranges for a lung to expand so that it can contract. It expands, therefore it contracts. The pair is one movement in two phases, and the second phase is legible in the first.

## Why the strategy reading collapses

If 固 meant "deliberately," the chapter would be telling you to bulk up your enemy before destroying him. Two things break immediately.

First, the same law would then apply to you: whoever is arranging your growth would be planning your collapse, and you would have no way to know. That is not a doctrine of power; it is a doctrine of universal paranoia.

Second, the chapter's own conclusion refuses it: 柔弱勝剛強. If the method is manipulation, the conclusion should be "cunning beats strength." Instead it says softness beats hardness — which is a statement about structure, not about tactics.

## 微明

> 是謂微明.

This is called the subtle clarity. 微 is fine, barely visible; 明 is the illumination from chapter 16 and 33.

The clarity is subtle because the pattern is never seen at the scale of a single event. You see the closing, not the opening that made it possible. The seeing requires holding both phases at once, which is what makes it 微 rather than obvious.

## 魚不可脫於淵

A fish cannot leave the deep.

The line seems to be a warning about exposure, and it is more specific than that: the fish's capacity depends on the medium. Remove it from the water and it does not become free; it becomes unable to move at all.

> 國之利器不可以示人.

The sharp instruments of the state are not to be displayed.

This is the practical consequence of 微明. A capability that is shown becomes a capability that is countered. Display converts a structural advantage into a contest, and contests are decided by force — which is the register the chapter is arguing against.

## What the chapter is actually for

34 said the Dao does not master. 35 said a person holds it inward and others come without harm. 36 supplies the eye: see the two phases as one movement, and then take your hand back.

The hand comes back because the movement does not need help. That is 柔弱勝剛強 — not that softness is stronger, but that the soft position does not have to spend anything to stay in the movement.

## A test

Find something currently at its peak — a trend, a person's influence, your own momentum. The chapter's claim is not that it will fall; it is that the falling is already in the rising, and the useful question is what you are holding on to.
